investigations.assessment: Confirmed display-name fidelity error in the selected sandbox: issuer_name and canonical_name are BlackRock Liquidity Funds Treasury, whereas the tagged printed investment row names BlackRock Liquidity Funds T-Fund - Institutional Class. This establishes a mismatch to the disclosed position label, not that the holding belongs to an economically unrelated manager or a different verified security. The filer itself supplied Treasury in the typed InvestmentIdentifierAxis domain; the pipeline retained that internal identifier as its displayed issuer. The actual HTML nonfraction facts f-2534 through f-2538 all bind to c-427 on the T-Fund row. No evidence of a wrong-row join, lost value, duplicate position, or comparative-period substitution was found in this selected population.
investigations.population_reconstruction: Read every issuer_name_printed row in rgA4/output/shadow/page_rule_findings.csv for this CIK: exactly one. Independently reran the unchanged candidate_rules load_rows/ledger_rows in memory against rgA4 holdings and field-status parquet: 341 tested rows at 2024-06-30, one finding, exact same row_id and not_the_printed_name kind. Blind share is 3/341 (two missing printed rows and one without comparable name); page test is not suppressed. These are detector population counts, not 341 manual source reviews. Diagnostic is scratch/2026-10-21_review_queue/0001911066/source.txt.

hypotheses_tested: Bad page association: rejected by direct original HTML facts f-2534 to f-2538, all referencing c-427 inside the T-Fund row, with matching rate, cost, fair value and net-assets percentage.
Comparative-period duplication or sibling confusion: rejected for selected population; XML c-427 is June 30, 2024 and the only context carrying the exact Treasury identifier in this filing.
Pipeline invented Treasury through normalization: rejected as the immediate mechanism; original typed member already says Treasury and published identifier, issuer_name and canonical_name retain it.

Prior narrative already reviewed this exact issue: checked 0001911066.md, reports/0001911066.json and decision entries D-084, D-123, D-182. They discuss comma splitting, rotated names, Dragon and cash-unit/classification defects, but do not assess this 2024-06-30 Treasury versus T-Fund mismatch. No further exclusion requested.

Share count is necessarily an extraction scale error: not established. Cash-schedule caption says dollar amounts in thousands; no exception explaining share scaling or printed per-unit price appears on this bounded cash table. Inline scale=3 and XML give 16,382,000, matching published shares. Printed 16,382 can represent thousands of units. No error or ambiguity finding is inferred from the raw-digit difference alone; source convention was not independently resolved.
